completion:
Identify those results that can be most plausibly explained in terms consistent with the hypothesis.
3. For the alternative outcomes, if there is variation in magnitude (e.g. positive effect in the non-critical groups, but a weak negative one in the critical group), pick the variation that is most marginal with respect to p-value.
4. Conduct smaller-scale post-hoc exploratory analyses in search of “significant” effects (e.g. when comparing the tail of a distribution, relative to the whole distribution).
5. Conduct a sufficient number of ad-hoc analyses on a sufficient number of outcome measures (e.g. conduct correlational, path, and partial correlation analyses on multiple measures of outcome variables).
6. Construct a selective narrative of the plausible results.
